title: One angle's search output (wave 1)
description: What a single integrations search child produces. `outcome` decides what else is owed.

angle_id.description: Resolved against the REGISTRY by `angle-unknown`, not pinned here -- the registry is the authority on which angles exist.

outcome.description: ran = cells, a bound, a retrieval_summary and any admitted candidates. not_run = NOTHING but not_run{map_verdict}. vacated = cells, their causes, vacated{cause} and a retrieval_summary; candidates and unadmitted are NOT owed, because recording either means a search happened.

map_verdict.description: The map's angle_applicability reason that ruled this angle out.

queries.description: Recorded VERBATIM, including any filter expression a catalog walk used.

count_frame.description: REQUIRED on any non-zero returned. A catalog count is unre-derivable without knowing whether it counted providers or APIs.

kept.description: How many distinct candidate ROWS this cell carried forward into candidates PLUS unadmitted. NEVER a result count.

cause.description: Required wherever status is not reached, and carrying observable evidence.

fallback_used.description: null, or a PREFIXED route: `angle:<row_id>` or `row:<row_id>`. Both prefixes name the LEVEL whose declaration was walked; the token is ALWAYS a registry source row, because an angle's declared fallback is itself a row id and no angle may fall back to another angle. fallback-declared compares the PARSED TARGET, never the raw token.

enumerated.description: true when the source was walked as a COMPLETE listing -- every entry examined, whatever term filter was then applied to the RESULTS. false when the TRAVERSAL itself was bounded by a cap, a cursor or a page limit. ABSENT where the source row's complete_listing is n/a. The distinction is the TRAVERSAL, not the query, and it is what makes a zero readable: an enumerated zero is evidence the service is absent from that catalog; a bounded zero is not.

bound.description: Owed on outcome:ran ALONE -- an angle that did not run bounded nothing.

cap.description: The registry's value for this angle, transcribed VERBATIM, or null where the registry declares no cap. The no-cap form is legal and `hit` is then false by construction. **It bounds the CARRIED ROWS -- candidates plus unadmitted -- and nothing else.** Not the summed `returned` across cells, and not any single cell's `returned`: a filter over an unbounded corpus can return any number of rows and the cap is a budget on what the angle RECORDS. The three readings agree only by accident, so the one that governs is stated here.

ordering.description: The registry's ordering_signal transcribed verbatim, or -- where the run did not apply it -- the ordering it DID apply, with the reason in ordering_deviation.

dropped_note.description: Required wherever hit is true: what fell off the end, so a reader can re-apply the ordering.

ordering_deviation.description: Why the applied ordering differs from the registry's.

retrieval_summary.description: Both DERIVED from the finished coverage list rather than counted as you go.

unadmitted.description: Every dropped candidate, with a real reason. A cross-catalog re-find of an already-recorded service is present_on[] ALONE and is NEVER an unadmitted row -- duplicate-of is reserved for two distinct NAMES resolving to one canonical host.

found_by.description: REQUIRED, because kept counts candidates PLUS unadmitted per cell and a row citing no cell breaks the arithmetic.

reason_class.description: no-first-party-home is admission conjunct (a); no-retrievable-corpus-row is conjunct (b).

item_id.description: The vendor host, lowercased (stripe.com), or NODOMAIN-<slug> where the service has no host of its own.

id_class.description: Which grammar item_id follows. The two disagreeing is refused.

found_by.description: The `group_id/source_id` CELL key of the coverage cell that produced this row.

homepage.description: The service's own first-party home. Carries the weight of admission conjunct (a), which a reviewer condition judges -- a gate that never fetches cannot.

category.description: A frozen-but-extensible VOCABULARY, not an enum -- seeded from the coordinator's union, and an out-of-seed value carries its provenance in notes[]. Calling it an enum would promise a closed set this type cannot close.

auth_scheme.description: An OAS 3.1 security-scheme type, or null where the catalog's auth_mode has no OAS member. NO enum: null must stay legal for exactly the rows §3.5 mandates, and an enum admitting null beside the vocabulary would admit it unconditionally. oas-auth-vocabulary is the rule that closes it.

oauth_flow.description: An OAS 3.1 OAuth flow name, and only against an oauth2 scheme. NO enum, for the same reason as auth_scheme.

http_scheme.description: The HTTP auth scheme name from the IANA registry, recorded VERBATIM as the descriptor spells it. NO enum: a JSON Schema enum is exact-match and would refuse `bearer` before the case-insensitive rule ran, leaving a correctly transcribed descriptor with no legal writing.

source_authority.description: The band of the source the LOCATOR points at -- the authority of the EVIDENCE, not of the cell that found the row. A row found in a catalog and quoted from the vendor's own page correctly carries first-party here.

locator.description: An absolute http(s) URL. That it RESOLVES and is the vendor's own is a reviewer condition; locator-resolvable checks only the syntax.

present_on.description: a1 ONLY: the source_ids whose catalog listed this service. The one wave-1 observation wave 2 cannot recover -- found_by is a single cell key, so a service in three catalogs is ONE row and the other two memberships have no other home. INCLUDES the found_by cell's own source_id: the list is the COMPLETE membership, not the membership minus the catalog that won.

rate_limit_documented.description: Tri-state: a vendor that documents NO limit is a real and distinguishable observation, not a missing value.

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim FROM the locator. Judged against `claim` by a reviewer condition; a rule joining the two would refuse exactly the honest case.

claim.description: What this survey asserts from the quote. The claim-versus-quote boundary is a reviewer condition.

provenance.description: External identifiers transcribed for a later wave, with no in-artifact counterpart to check them against.
